# venice-bridge

> venice-bridge is a free, open-source local bridge for macOS that lets OpenCode, Claude Code, Codex CLI and other OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible coding agents use a venice.ai web subscription, with working tool calls.

## What it does

- The bridge (`venice_bridge.py`) runs an OpenAI Chat Completions server on `127.0.0.1:18891` (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, `GET /v1/models`, `GET /health`, `GET /stats`, `POST /reload`, `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`, image tools (`POST /v1/images/generations`, `/v1/images/edits`, `/v1/image/upscale`, `/v1/image/background-remove`, `GET /v1/image/styles`; 0-credit models only unless `VENICE_ALLOW_CREDIT_IMAGES=1`)); chat accepts base64 image and document attachments.
- The optional adapter (`venice_adapters.py`, standard library only) runs on `127.0.0.1:18892` and serves Anthropic Messages (`POST /v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`) for Claude Code and OpenAI Responses (`POST /v1/responses`) for Codex CLI, translating them to Chat Completions for the bridge.
- The `claude-venice` launcher runs the Claude Code CLI on the adapter in an isolated profile (`~/.claude-venice`); it skips Claude Code's permission prompts by default (`VENICE_CLAUDE_SKIP_PERMS=0` turns that off).
- Forwards requests to the venice.ai web app's own backend, signed in with the user's browser login (the `__client` cookie of `clerk.venice.ai`). It does not use the paid Venice API and needs no API key (the launcher's `--venice-api` / `--claude` backends are opt-in and metered).
- `VENICE_BRIDGE_ROUTE=auto` (default) uses Venice's plain chat route, where no Venice agent loop swallows tool calls, and falls back to the agent route for a model the chat route does not know; `chat` and `agent` force one route.
- Emulates tool calling in text: the tool list goes into the prompt, and a tolerant parser plus native and tagged call readers turn the model's reply into OpenAI `tool_calls`; foreign tool and argument names are routed to the client's tools. Includes retries, a completion check, a stream gate, and an optional early-stop judge.
- A model id `<backend>/<model>` (e.g. `ollama/qwen3:8b`, `lmstudio/<id>`) goes straight to a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, MLX via `~/.config/venice-bridge/backends.json`), with no Venice login or quota.
- Opt-in Venice web search per request (`<model>:web`, `<model>:xsearch`) or process-wide (`VENICE_WEB=1`, `VENICE_X_SEARCH=1`); off by default.
- Opt-in reasoning (chat route) for requests without tools only: model suffix `:think` (aliases `:reason`, `:reasoning`), `VENICE_REASONING=1`, or `reasoning_effort` `medium` / `high`; the chain of thought comes back as `reasoning_content`. All three are ignored when tools are declared, so reasoning has no effect in agent loops.
- `GET /v1/models` lists only models the web subscription covers (no credit models, no `e2ee-*`; `VENICE_EXCLUDE_MODELS` hides more by glob), plus a virtual `venice-auto` model: a Venice model normally, the first local model in `VENICE_AUTO_MODELS` (default `ollama/qwen3:8b`) while the daily quota is used up. The request that hits the limit still fails once.
- An in-memory response cache answers byte-identical repeat requests without a Venice call (`VENICE_BRIDGE_CACHE=0` disables it).

## Install

- Requirements: macOS, Python 3.10+, `pip install curl_cffi` (or `pipx install venice-bridge` from PyPI), a venice.ai web account (tested on a paid plan, Pro).
- Save the cookie value to `~/.config/venice-bridge/client-cookie.txt` (mode 0600).
- Run `python3 venice_bridge.py`, then check `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18891/health`. For Claude Code or Codex also run `python3 venice_adapters.py`.
- Self-checks (offline): `python3 test_venice_bridge.py` and `python3 test_venice_adapters.py`.

## Use

- OpenCode: copy the provider block from `examples/opencode.json` into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, then `opencode -m venice-bridge/deepseek-v4-1-flash-uncensored`.
- Claude Code: `claude-venice` or `claude-venice -m <venice-model-id>`.
- Codex CLI: a command-line provider with `base_url="http://127.0.0.1:18892/v1"` and `wire_api="responses"` (full command in the README).
- Any OpenAI-compatible client: base URL `http://127.0.0.1:18891/v1`, any placeholder API key; from Docker, `http://host.docker.internal:18891/v1`.
- Autostart on macOS with the launchd templates `examples/com.example.venice-bridge.plist` and `examples/com.example.venice-adapters.plist`.

## Limits

- Unofficial; not affiliated with Venice.ai. Uses undocumented web endpoints that can change at any time.
- Automating a logged-in web session may be against Venice's terms of service; use only your own account.
- Tested on a paid plan (Pro). The agent route needs a paid plan (a free account gets `403 creator_access_required`); a free account has a very small chat quota.
- The web plan is limited by a daily request quota, not tokens; reported token counts are estimates.
- macOS only so far. Codex's namespace tools (MCP, multi-agent) and built-in `web_search` do not pass through the adapter.
- With tools, short replies are sent only when complete. Tool calling is emulated; Venice's fast models are weak at long agentic chains and need their work checked.
